root_cause.text: The cpufreq governor error path in cpufreq_dbs_governor_init() performed manual gov->exit()/kfree(dbs_data) cleanup after kobject_init_and_add() failure even though kobject_put() already triggered the dbs_data kobject release callback cpufreq_dbs_data_release() to free the same dbs_data object.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the direct gov->exit(dbs_data) call after kobject_put(&dbs_data->attr_set.kobj) and replaces it with a jump, while the CVE/commit text explicitly states that cpufreq_dbs_data_release() invoked by kobject_put() calls gov->exit(dbs_data) and kfree(dbs_data), and the old error path then called them again, causing a double free.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes the direct gov->exit(dbs_data) call after kobject_put(&dbs_data->attr_set.kobj) and replaces it with a jump, while the CVE/commit text explicitly states that cpufreq_dbs_data_release() invoked by kobject_put() calls gov->exit(dbs_data) and kfree(dbs_data), and the old error path then called them again, causing a double free.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the governor-init failure cleanup path by using kobject_put()-driven teardown and jumping to the shared policy cleanup logic instead of calling gov->exit() directly.
intent_record.what: In the initialization failure path of cpufreq_dbs_governor_init(), the direct call to gov->exit(dbs_data) was removed, kobject_put(&dbs_data->attr_set.kobj) was moved to occur after clearing governor_data and possibly gov->gdbs_data, and execution now jumps to the existing free_policy_dbs_info label instead of continuing into free_dbs_data.
intent_record.how: This changes cleanup sequencing on kobject initialization failure so that object release is driven through kobject_put() and the function reuses the common rollback path for freeing policy-related state, avoiding an immediate gov->exit(dbs_data) call that could conflict with kobject-managed teardown or skip needed cleanup.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the governor-init failure cleanup path by using kobject_put()-driven teardown and jumping to the shared policy cleanup logic instead of calling gov->exit() directly.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes the cpufreq governor init error cleanup path to rely on kobject_put()-triggered release instead of manual gov->exit()/free-style teardown, preventing the double cleanup of dbs_data.

candidates.rationale: This manual teardown is the core bug: after kobject_put() on dbs_data, the kobject release callback can already free dbs_data, so calling gov->exit(dbs_data) here can operate on an object that is already being released and contributes to double cleanup.
This directly frees dbs_data again on the error path even though kobject_put() already triggers the cpufreq_dbs_data_release() callback to free the same object, causing the double-free.
This invokes the kobject release path that frees dbs_data; the vulnerability arises because subsequent manual cleanup incorrectly assumes dbs_data still needs explicit gov->exit()/kfree teardown.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct double-free in the error path. After kobject_put(&dbs_data->attr_set.kobj);, the dbs_data kobject release callback can already free dbs_data, so this explicit kfree(dbs_data); frees the same object again.

This performs manual teardown on dbs_data after kobject_put() has already initiated kobject-based release of the same object. That can lead to use-after-free or duplicate cleanup as part of the same faulty error path.
